proposal.title: 1978–79 external peripherals — printers and plotting equipment 1
proposal.reason: Import 10 distinct commercial identities from research items 19, 20, 21, 22, 29, 30, 40, 50, 94, 95. Describe the native host boundary and assess product and core-standard impacts at 1979-12-31. Dedicated memory and other unrelated accessories explicitly carry no direct impact. Conditional comparisons do not establish qualified adapters, provider adoption or measured sales. Prices and cumulative sales remain editorial evidence, outside foundation and the annual-sales model. See the per-item evidence in data_storytelling/review_evidence/external-peripherals-1979/assessment.json. Revised for explicit product/standard relationships: consolidate descriptions into specification, relocate impact prose, compare canonical implementation boundaries and retain source/qualification limits. Historical documentation cannot establish fictional implementations or measured adoption. Per-record evidence: data_storytelling/review_evidence/external-impact-revision/assessment.json.

parameters.value: Heath and suitably interfaced serial micros

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Assess {historical_product} in its recorded {host} configuration. Compare usable printer configurations with their actual interface, driver, paper and output requirements.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: Parallel/serial printing is not FlexiBUS. A bridge would need device identification, status mapping, backpressure and protection against duplicate output after uncertain retries. The relationship concerns alternative complete configurations, not proven direct compatibility with this standard.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: A broad established printer choice can weaken the incentive to adopt a bus with a narrower qualified range. A validated bridge could broaden that range, but neither a bridge delivery nor higher sales is assumed.

parameters.value: Heath and suitably interfaced serial micros

impacted_products.assumption_description: Assess the recorded {host} configuration with its required controller, cabling and software. Impact dot-matrix hardcopy peripheral supplied as a kit.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The alternative combines the MPI MP40 mechanism with a FlexiBUS device controller. Compare actual print width, character repertoire, quality, paper handling and qualified driver support; the current definition establishes no universal speed or output-quality advantage. The canonical implementation is {implementation}.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: The printer is an alternative hardcopy purchase where the host supplies its required interface and driver. Width, output quality, throughput and consumables can favour it for different jobs; it cannot connect directly to FlexiBUS. This is a conditional purchase-path assessment, not evidence of measured market share or superior performance.
